newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly firmer, PGMs do well.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly firmer, PGMs do well.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly firmer Tuesday, helped by fund shortcovering and forecasts for a tighter platinum group metals market from refiner Johnson Matthey.

"Gold, platinum and palladium all did well, providing confirmation of the gains Monday, with funds doing more covering of short positions, but there's likely to be producer sell orders waiting around $385-386 in gold," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said.
COMEX December gold ended up 60 cents at $383.40, after seeing a session high at $383.80, a 10-day high.
Spot gold ended quoted $382.20/283.70, up from the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $381.90, and the New York close Monday at $381.50/381.90.
"If this (upward) momentum can be sustained, a test of the $384.00-385.00 resistance cannot be ruled out," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.

Spot gold has recovered to near the top of its downtrend channel since August on the daily charts, and on the weekly charts, is testing resistance near the top of the longer term downtrend from the five year highs at $417 in February 1996, analysts said.
"Possibly bullish chart patterns and hedger buying of gold can't be ignored," MCM analyst Peter McTeague said.

"There's been good buying under $380 in recent weeks, but large traders ("non-commercials" in the CFTC Commitment of Traders Report for week ended November 5) are net short 53,706 contracts, with 43 large traders net short, the most since late 1994."
Total COMEX open interest in both gold and silver has slipped in the past few days, as funds have covered some positions, analysts said.
COMEX December silver ended down 1.3 cent at $4.880 an ounce, after seeing an intraday high at $4.910, a ten day high.
The spot/gold silver ratio edged back up to 78.3 by the close, from 77.9 at Monday's close, with silver weaker than gold.
NYMEX January platinum ended up $1.00 at $391.80 an ounce, after seeing an intraday high at $393.80, its highest level since mid-September.
NYMEX December palladium closed up $1.95 at $1.20 an ounce, after seeing a ten day high at $120.75..

Earlier Johnson Matthey, the world's largest refiner of platinum group metals, released its forecasts for 1996 supply and demand, which suggested the surplus supply of platinum would shrink this year to 80,000 ounces from 190,000 ounces last year.
Meanwhile, Johnson Matthey saw the supply of palladium moving into a deficit this year of 130,000 ounces from a surplus last year of 240,000 ounces.
